Expand across()/if_any()/if_all() dots at the quosure level

Source: R/across.R
expand_across_dots.Rd

Walks dots in order; a top-level, unnamed across(...) dot is replaced by expand_one_across()'s (possibly multi-element, possibly empty) result, a top-level if_any(...)/if_all(...) dot is replaced by expand_if_any_all()'s single folded quosure (keeping the ORIGINAL dot's own name, if any – e.g. mutate(flag = if_any(...))), and every other dot is passed through unchanged. across() is disallowed as a top-level filter() dot (matching real dplyr 1.2.1 exactly, verified empirically – it raises at EVALUATION time there, not parse time, but the message ("must be a logical vector... use if_any()/if_all() instead") is the same either way, so raising it up front here is equivalent and cheaper). A NAMED top-level across() dot (e.g. mutate(z = across(x, y))) packs a data-frame column and never gets here: dots_need_fallback() sends the whole call to the CPU fallback.

Usage

expand_across_dots(dots, schema, group_cols, verb)

Arguments

dots

A list of quosures (already past cur_group_id substitution, if applicable)

schema

Current schema

group_cols

Character vector, the effective group columns to exclude from .cols's selectable universe

verb

Character, "filter"/"mutate"/"summarise"/"transmute"

Value

A new (possibly longer, possibly shorter) named list of quosures, with the "needs_fallback" attribute described above, and a "provenance" attribute: list(origin, kind), one entry per returned quosure. origin is the index of the input dot it came from; kind is "dot" (the input dot, passed through unchanged), "across" (an expansion of an unnamed across() dot, staged or not) or "combined" (an if_any()/if_all() dot). mutate()/transmute() use it to tell which original dot a value computed from the expanded dots belongs to. When an expansion names a column, col is the column each one stands for (a staged one's, not its temp's; an if_any()/if_all()'s first; "" for a plain dot), which the errors name (#30).

Details

Expansion stops at the first dot that needs dplyr (the result is then partial and only its "needs_fallback" attribute is meaningful).

The result carries a "needs_fallback" attribute. It is TRUE when the schema or the .fns values show that dplyr must run the call: an unsupported .fns/extra-argument shape (a non-inlinable lambda, a value whose free variables are columns, ...), duplicate output names, or, in summarise()/filter(), an across() that renames onto a column that a later expansion of the same across() reads (across(c(y = x, z = y), ...)): dplyr evaluates every function against the pre-across() data, while the expanded dots would run in sequence. That needs the schema, so dots_need_fallback() can't see it; the verb calls then re-run the ORIGINAL dots on the CPU. In mutate()/transmute() the same hazard is staged instead: the expansions are computed into temp columns first and assigned afterwards, and the "staged_temps" attribute names the temps the caller must drop (and whose CPU fallbacks must use the ORIGINAL dots).
